A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain complete main texts and appendices A-L. Their methods, equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be reliably matched; a localized caption overlap in v2 does not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original style-mimicry experiments and human evaluations across ten artists, with numerical results in Tables 1 and 3 and supplementary experiments throughout the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and additionally reports human preferences for original versus preprocessed artwork in Appendix K.2.

M1.justification: The Gaussian noising, DiffPure, Noisy Upscaling, and IMPRESS++ procedures remain unchanged, including their components, objectives, and sampling procedures in Section 4.3 and Appendix I.

E1.justification: Appendix K.2 adds a clean-art test scenario: directly evaluating original artwork after Noisy Upscaling, without downstream mimicry generation. The source datasets and artist pool remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated protections and comparison methods remain the same, including the Glaze 2.0 and Mist v2 experiments already present in v1. Glaze 2.1 is newly discussed but has no reported experimental comparison.

E3.justification: The newly reported Appendix K.2 control compares original and preprocessed artwork for six existing artists and specifies two held-out original artworks per artist. The main experiment's training settings, prompts, evaluation metrics, and annotation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix K.2 adds a targeted analysis of whether preprocessing itself damages artwork quality or style. Existing component illustrations, failure cases, artist-level analyses, and updated-protection experiments remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five annotators per comparison, randomized generation seeds, and the inter-annotator agreement analysis. The added control reports aggregate preferences without introducing confidence intervals, repeated-run information, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Appendix K.2 newly reports preferences for preprocessed originals of 50% for quality and 48.3% for style. Tables 1 and 3 retain their numerical values. Figures 11-15 also revise method and baseline/protected attributions for unchanged example images.

T1.justification: The threat model, success-rate definition, and mathematical objectives and derivations in Equations (1)-(9) are retained. No formal assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and central conclusion remain unchanged, but v2's introduction now states that Glaze 2.1 protects against the specific attacks described. This adds a limited qualification to the claims about existing protections, although the abstract retains its blanket wording.

C2.justification: v2 explains unsuccessful artist recruitment and qualifies the relevance of MTurk judgments. It interprets the new control as showing little preprocessing damage, adds an explanation of complementary mimicry methods, and removes the categorical recommendation that having no protection tools is preferable to having insecure ones.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, hardware, execution times, and code/data access information remain unchanged, particularly in Appendices J and L. The added study design is covered under E3.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work survey are retained. The acknowledgment that Glaze 2.1 responds to the presented attacks makes a limited update to the paper's positioning relative to protection tools.

P1.justification: There are localized revisions to the introduction, participant justification, results explanation, and ethics discussion, plus the new Appendix K.2 subsection. The overall organization and most prose remain intact; conference headings and correspondence formatting also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference formatting, relocates Figure 4, and revises column labels in Figures 11-15, including replacing incorrect Gaussian-noising labels with the methods already identified in their captions. The images remain unchanged. On page 40, Figure 33 newly overlaps part of Figure 32's caption.

improvement.justification: The added preprocessing control addresses a previously untested quality tradeoff, while corrected figure labels and clearer recruitment and Glaze 2.1 qualifications improve interpretability and transparency. These are limited gains because the main experiments remain unchanged and the broad abstract claim persists. They outweigh the localized caption overlap introduced on page 40.
